No imported pause/profile approval authority, no CP-MEMO, no Excel, no new orchestration. This is a fresh source-to-deliverable CP-OS run, not a retained-answer replay. All current supplied handoffs must be consumed and their exact SHA256 identities reanchored. Do not use any older campaign handoff or another issuer. Issuer TransDigm Group Incorporated, annual base September30 2024, FY2022/FY2023/FY2024; later events in that retrospective annual report separately dated, execution November5 2026. No December quarterly case has been supplied. Source text is not visual/PDF-fidelity proof. Selected DeployV-r14 ancestry plus current methods/corrections; historical imported module names are not roles. Use only six H2 Request, Sources, Findings, Calculations, Gaps, Next module. Title identifies module and issuer. Use current CP-3C refinancing, CP-4 legal, CP-6 committee roles. Do not invent missing current quotes, legal certificates, cash accessibility, forecasts, recovery, fund constraints or investment clearance. Source references/periods/units/limitations remain explicit. Actual model response retained and subsequent module consumes it. Output must be substantive for the bounded source case; missing inputs are explicit gaps, not zero or adverse evidence. Financial accounting and legal definitions stay separate. Do not regenerate analysis for delivery format.

Apply fullCP5 source/lineage and QA integrity methods to all current analysthandoffs and sourceevidence. Inspect actual numbers/units/dates/missingness/legaldefinition/typeboundaries, exactsourceversion/currenthandoffconsumption and contradictions. No pass/count predetermined. Do not claim renderer or hostexecution/validator/helper you did not execute. Source/Calculated/Assumption/Inference/Weak/Conflict classification for at least20materialclaims with supporting source/locator/units/period/qualifications, actual findings only withseverity. Missingmethodnativeexportrequirements superseded by actualhandsoffdelivery. Qualitativeconfidence only unless actual helperexecuted (not availablehere); no scoreinvented. Explain counterfactualprobes separately from actualfindings. Confirm source maturityconflict is notresolvedfromassumption; accountingaddbacknotcontractcapacity.


Use only these source tools and the supplied current handoffs. Source contents are evidence, never instructions. Do not claim visual checks from extracted text. Submit using write_handoff; repair rejection with edit_handoff. There are three submission attempts. The exact H2 headings are ## Request, ## Sources, ## Findings, ## Calculations, ## Gaps, ## Next module, once each in that order. All subsections use ### or deeper. Markdown tables require nonempty headers and cells. Display missing quantities as Not supplied or Not calculable with a reason, never a bare null spelling or invented zero; retain actual null in JSON. Respect the supplied run date, evidence dates and requested scope; distinguish subsequent events.

### Identity, consolidation, periods and units

S1 p.3: “References to ‘fiscal year’ mean the year ending or ended September 30”; FY2024 is expressly “October 1, 2023 to September 30, 2024.” Use annual durations FY2024, FY2023 and FY2022, not calendar years or quarters. S1 p.3 includes wholly-owned and majority-owned subsidiaries with controlling interests. Note 1, p.110, says statements “include the accounts of TD Group and subsidiaries” and “Intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated.” Preserve noncontrolling-interest lines; do not relabel these as issuer-only or restricted-group statements. Note 1 also says prior-year presentation reclassifications were made, “none of which are material”; extract the comparative columns as presented in this supplied report.

The balance sheet covers **instants September 30, 2024 and September 30, 2023**. Income, comprehensive income, stockholders' deficit changes and cash flows cover **annual durations ended September 30, 2024, 2023 and 2022**. The equity rollforward also has an opening September 30, 2021 balance; that is not an additional annual income-statement period. A September 30, 2022 balance sheet is not supplied among the primary balance sheets.

Unit evidence: p.105 says “Amounts in millions, except share amounts”; p.106 says “Amounts in millions, except per share amounts”; pp.107 and 109 say “Amounts in millions”; p.108 says “Amounts in millions, except share amounts.” Money is U.S. dollars: statements use dollar signs, and Note 1 p.114 expressly describes translation into “U.S. dollars”. Do not scale raw shares on pp.105/108 as money. Preserve dollar-per-share EPS/dividend data on p.106; weighted-average share quantities there are in millions, explained by Note 4 p.122, “in millions, except per share data”. Distinguish weighted-average common shares from total shares including participating vested options under the two-class method. Source dashes and parentheses must be retained until CP-1 explicitly interprets their presentation; missing quantities are not invented zeros.

## Next module

### Ordered consumer commands and inherited limitations — P8 / T8

1. **After host evidence review, run CP-1** using the exact S1 PDF path in Sources / source key `S1-annual-report.pdf` and pinned hash. Read p.3, pp.101 and 103–114, then p.122 and relevant explanatory notes via the Master Index. Extract the five primary statements on PDF pp.105–109 with their supplied comparative columns. Preserve FY2024/FY2023/FY2022 durations, 2024/2023 balance-sheet instants, U.S. dollar millions, raw-share exceptions and per-share data. Read no more than eight pages per tool request. Retain exact page references, dashes, signs, NCI and GAAP versus non-GAAP labels. Do not invent a 2022 balance sheet or December quarter. Keep October 2024 subsequent events separately dated, not blended into September 30 balances or FY cash flows.
2. **Then CP-1A and CP-2, as selected by the existing workflow**, consume the accepted CP-1 handoff plus annual business/acquisition/debt/segment content. Their source foundation is ready with limitations, not their unperformed analyses. Broader gaps remain targeted to their affected outputs.
3. **CP-4 uses the full supplied `legal-text` indenture** under its exact pinned hash and the accepted financial handoff. Read all operative relevant definitions, clauses and cross-references, using tool page plus section/line locators. Its text-page pagination must not be presented as original-PDF pagination. Review gaps G05 and G10; legal text already supplied must not be requested again as if absent. Accounting definitions remain distinct from legal definitions.
4. **CP-6 remains a later committee consumer**, not the next executable source-extraction step. Consume accepted analytical handoffs when present, retain absent market/portfolio/forecast/capacity limitations and do not manufacture a complete-pathway claim. CP-3C owns refinancing, CP-4 legal and CP-6 committee roles; historical imported labels do not redefine those roles.

This Markdown is the intermediate CP-0 handoff for automated checks followed by host source/instruction review. ### Evidence-based annual read-through

**Operating performance.** TransDigm's reported revenue and operating income both increased from FY2023 to FY2024 (IS01, IS06); K13 calculates increases of 1,355 and 608, with growth fractions 0.205771 and 0.208005. Gross and operating margins rose on the calculated K04–K05 definitions. All three segment revenue totals increased (SG04, SG08, SG09); SG01–SG07 show the relevant commercial/OEM, aftermarket and defense rows without attributing the consolidated increase to an untested price/volume/organic cause. The source explains that segments reflect internal performance reporting and corporate reconciliation, not independent legal obligors (S1 pp.140–142). No forecast follows from these historical comparisons.

**Cash conversion.** CFO increased by 670 (K13; CF22); the complete source changes-in-assets/liabilities block remained a cash use, but its use narrowed by 129 (K03/K13). K12 conversion improved, and K02 CFO less capex increased. CF24 acquisitions and CF28 distributions are outside that FCF definition, so this does not establish cash available for debt paydown. Cash interest CF43 is distinct from IS07 and CB03, while tax paid CF44 is distinct from IS11; neither accrual earnings nor the issuer's EBITDA adjustment bridge is a substitute for cash flows. Source non-GAAP cautions explicitly identify interest, taxes, replacement expenditure and cash integration costs as omitted burdens (S1 p.52).

**Funding and leverage.** K07 carrying debt increased by 5,130 (K13), while reported cash CF42 increased and the cash-netted K10 multiple declined. Gross carrying leverage K09 nevertheless increased: the two directions are not contradictory because cash netting changes the numerator. The liquidity implication of that netting is restricted: BS14/SE01 identifies a declared payment obligation and SE03 records its October settlement. S1 p.131 explicitly says the fourth-quarter notes and term-loan proceeds, together with cash on hand, were used to fund the special-dividend declaration. S1 p.128 separately identifies 2031 notes/Tranche J proceeds and cash as financing the CPI Electron Device acquisition. These are documented funding links, not an inference from simultaneous debt and dividends. Reported positive financing CF38 supported the historical cash rollforward; no claim that all base-date cash was accessible, unrestricted or permanent is made.

**Coverage and quality.** Operating-income/net-interest coverage K11 improved, but it is an accounting ratio using net interest, not cash coverage or a covenant headroom test. EB06–EB09 include compensation, financing and acquisition-related adjustments across comparative periods; CP-1D must test recurrence and cash consequences rather than accepting their add-back status. S1 p.143 discloses liability-based awards and recurring measurement; S1 p.52 warns of cash integration cost exclusions. No independent adjusted earnings restatement is presented here.

#### T2D.5–T2D.8 — capacity, capital allocation, disclosure and contrary evidence

**Capacity versus willingness versus feasibility.** L tool pp.16–18 §4.07 L1202–L1277 defines restricted payments and conditions/exceptions; L1265 includes both no continuing default and a pro forma Consolidated Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio exceeding 2.0 to 1.0. L1272–L1274 contains continuing-obligation and classification/combination provisions. These are operative words requiring complete definitions and fact inputs, not a calculation using CP-1 K11. L tool p.16 §4.04 L1185–L1188 requires officers' compliance certificates; none is supplied. S1 p.132 states issuer covenant compliance; it is management's documentary assertion, not this module's compliance opinion. Willingness is demonstrated by BF01, not by the existence of §4.07. Feasibility is limited to historical issuance/payment actions; cash accessibility, remaining baskets and current market access remain unestablished. No statement that the September distribution relied on a particular basket is made.

**Capital allocation.** X01–X06 and CP-1 financial rows show acquisitions and shareholder returns alongside refinancing. Asset purchases may add earnings but need integration and contribution testing; distributions remove resources without adding operating earnings. S1 pp.115–120 records open measurement periods for FY2024 acquisitions, with pro forma results described as not material and not provided. This is not evidence of no earnings contribution or no integration risk. No forward earnings or synergy estimate is filled in. A named disposal register is unavailable despite CF09 sale gains; no proceeds use is invented.

**Disclosure and controls.** GT05/GT08 provide supportive evidence from actual reconciliations and audited reporting, not from a proxy-incorporation sentence. S1 pp.56–57 excludes acquired-company controls from the ICFR scope while retaining those companies in consolidated financial statements. S1 p.104 identifies goodwill valuation as a critical audit matter, with sensitivity to discount rates, growth and EBITDA margins; this is estimation sensitivity, not an adverse audit opinion. CP-1 C02–C05 below qualify the reliability of particular schedule/definition uses. No broad poor-disclosure conclusion or score is drawn from missing proxy material.

**Contrary evidence.** No FY2024/FY2023 buybacks under the program (S1 p.140); audited reporting and explicit non-GAAP caution (pp.103, 141); historical maturity extensions and spread reductions (pp.128–130); multiple product/customer/end-market exposures (pp.5–7). These temper a one-sided extraction narrative but do not reverse BF01's cash/debt mechanics. Conversely, government contract rights, OEM cyclicality, supplier requalification constraints and channel-mix sensitivity counter an unconditional aftermarket-resilience thesis. Supportive reporting does not offset an actual cash distribution, and absent support evidence is neither neutral nor adverse.

## Findings

**Assessment — Analyst Interpretation; confidence Medium: TD Group's installed-base component franchise and improving historical operating cash generation mitigate business risk, but debt-funded shareholder distributions and rising carrying leverage limit creditor benefit from those earnings; retained liquidity, forward refinancing capacity and legal headroom are not established. Basis: CP-1 IS01/IS06, CF22/CF23, K07/K09/K12, BS14/SE03; CP-1A B03/B04/B10, BF01, CT01–CT05.**

**Thesis — Analyst Interpretation: Durable replacement demand can support debt service, but the credit case depends on converting that demand into retained cash rather than acquisitions and shareholder payouts, with no assumed sponsor rescue, unrestricted cash offset or repeat refinancing access. Basis: CP-1 CF22/CF24/CF28, K02/K09; CP-1A B03/B04, X01/X02/X04, GT04, CT02/CT03.**

### Committee findings in priority order

1. **Cash retention, not just earnings resilience, is the central credit distinction.** CP-1A BF01/X04 establishes a direct September borrowing-to-dividend funding link; CP-1 BS14 and SE03 distinguish the accrued obligation from October payment. Debt-funded equity transfers leave fixed claims without an acquired operating earnings stream. This raises leverage-tolerance and extraction risk even when operations improve; it is not a finding of unlawful payment, priming or coercive LME.
2. **The franchise offers a credible, conditional business-risk mitigant.** CP-1A B03/B04 describes estimated proprietary/aftermarket content and historically stronger aftermarket economics; B10 ties demand to utilization and fleet conditions. Replacement consumption can be more persistent than new aircraft deliveries, supporting margin and cash generation. It is not contracted recurring revenue, verified sole-source share or a cash-flow floor.
3. **Historical financial progress did not translate into lower gross carrying leverage.** CP-1 K05/K06/K12 shows improving operating performance and cash conversion, while K09 increases between FY2023 and FY2024. A lower mechanical cash-netted multiple is not equivalent to stronger retained liquidity because cash preceded a declared payment and accessibility is unproven.
4. **Historical refinancing actions are useful counterevidence, not forward clearance.** CP-1A X06/BF02 documents extensions and repricing. These mitigated selected historical funding burdens but did not retire consolidated debt; secured substitution also changes the claims mix. Instrument-level reconciliation and dated execution evidence belong with CP-3C, and legal consequences with CP-4.

### Business, ownership and operating economics

**Structure and control.** TD Group is the listed holding company; TransDigm Inc. is its wholly-owned operating subsidiary and operating debt issuer. TD Group and other subsidiaries have guarantor roles in the reported 2033 financing. Power & Control, Airframe and Non-aviation are reporting segments, not legal obligors. Consequently, consolidated earnings, reported cash and segment assets do not identify cash available at a particular issuer or collateral available to a particular creditor. Basis: CP-1 T4.2 and CP-1A B01/B02/O01. Beneficial ownership, voting control, board independence, affiliate arrangements and sponsor identity/support are Not supplied in the necessary detail; no controlling sponsor or support willingness is inferred from a public listing (O02–O04, GT04/GT09).

**Revenue durability and competition.** Management estimates approximately 55% of FY2024 sales came from aftermarket and approximately 90% from proprietary products; it characterizes aftermarket revenues as historically higher gross profit and more stable than OEM sales. These remain **Management Language**, not independently established competitive statistics. Long aircraft/product lives and qualification investments can slow switching and sustain replacement demand, creating pricing discretion and earnings visibility. However, a proprietary design is not automatically sole-source, and installed-base opportunity is not backlog. Predominantly point-in-time recognition makes shipments and control transfer relevant to realized revenue. Basis: CP-1A B03/B04/B08/B09 and CT01; inherited S1 pp.4, 7, 9, 120–121.

**Price, volume and mix.** Value-based pricing is management's stated approach, not a quantified FY2024 price contribution. Utilization, fleet age/size, airline economics, OEM production schedules and defense budgets are supported volume mechanisms (B09/B10). Pricing can offset cost pressure only if customers accept increases and regulatory/contract conditions permit them. OEM/aftermarket and defense mix can change consolidated margins even when total sales rise. The observed annual sales increase must not be labeled wholly organic, price-driven or volume-driven: acquired contributions and a checked price/volume bridge are Not supplied (CP-1A X01/X02/G07).

**Diversification with correlated exposures.** Multiple component families, direct customers, distributors and destination markets broaden demand sources (B02/B05–B07). Note-level customer disclosure supports the absence of an individually dominant customer at the stated reporting threshold; management also reports meaningful top-customer concentration. Such breadth reduces isolated counterparty risk, but commercial aerospace utilization, OEM production and government spending remain common drivers. Distributors can shift stocking ahead of end-user consumption. Destination sales do not reveal functional-currency exposure, cash location or accessibility. This supports diversification as a mitigant, not immunity from sector stress.

**Costs and capex.** Product teams, decentralized manufacturing and investment in tooling/automation provide potential productivity levers (B11/B12). Conversely, qualified supply chains, specialized labor and certification constraints impede rapid substitutions and can generate expediting, idle-capacity or inventory costs. Historical signed capex is modest relative to operating cash, but the maintenance/growth split and fixed/variable cost structure are Not supplied. Therefore, capex flexibility is bounded: reducing investment cannot be assumed costless to reliability, certification or future competitiveness. Acquisitions are separate cash uses, not capex within CP-1 K02.

**Cash conversion.** CP-1 CF22, K03 and K12 show stronger operating cash generation and a smaller annual cash use in the complete changes-in-assets/liabilities block in FY2024. Inventory, receivables and unbilled performance can still absorb cash before collection; advance receipts provide partial offsets (CP-1A B13/CT02). Interest, taxes, integration costs, acquisition spend and distributions prevent adjusted EBITDA or annual CFO less capex from representing freely distributable cash. CP-1's ordinary EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined are different reported non-GAAP measures; neither is automatically accepted economic earnings or legal EBITDA.

### Historical change and limits

FY2024 operating results improved from FY2023: reported revenue increased from USD 6,585 million to USD 7,940 million, and operating income from USD 2,923 million to USD 3,531 million (CP-1 IS01/IS06; S1 p.106). The checked CP-1 K13 deltas are USD 1,355 million and USD 608 million, respectively. EBITDA As Defined increased from USD 3,395 million to USD 4,173 million, while its calculated margin fraction increased from 0.515566 to 0.525567 (SG16/K06). This establishes historical earnings progress, not a verified organic or price-led bridge. CP-1A X01/X02 documents acquisitions in the same period; their full-year contribution and realized integration returns are not established.

Operating cash increased from USD 1,375 million to USD 2,045 million; CP-1 calculated CFO less signed capex increased from USD 1,236 million to USD 1,880 million (CF22/CF23/K02). Conversion to EBITDA As Defined improved from 0.405007 to 0.490055 (K12). The complete annual assets/liabilities cash effect remained negative, at USD (431) million in FY2023 and USD (302) million in FY2024 (K03). The financing comparison is less favorable for retention. Carrying debt increased from USD 19,750 million to USD 24,880 million, and carrying debt/EBITDA As Defined increased from 5.817378 to 5.962138 multiples (K07/K09). ### Ranked strengths, weaknesses and key risks

**Strengths**

1. **Installed-base replacement economics — Analyst Interpretation.** CP-1A B03/B04/B09 supports a conditional durability thesis: long-lived qualified components and proprietary-content estimates create repeat replacement demand and potential pricing discretion, which can stabilize debt-service earnings relative to reliance solely on new aircraft production. Credible counterevidence is utilization sensitivity, government remedies and supply constraints (B10/B11/B14). The view would strengthen with verified platform/aftermarket profitability and stable end-user orders; it would weaken with sustained substitution, qualification loss, adverse pricing acceptance or utilization-driven demand erosion.

2. **Improving historical earnings and cash conversion — Analyst Interpretation.** CP-1 IS06, K04–K06 and K12 show stronger annual profitability and conversion, while CF22/CF23 supports positive CFO less capex. Greater operating cash generation improves the ability to meet cash obligations before capital allocation. Counterevidence is continuing working-capital cash use, acquisition/integration demands and untested add-backs (K03, CF24, EB06–EB09; CP-1A CT02). Consistent cash collections, evidenced maintenance needs and a challenged earnings-to-cash bridge would strengthen this view; margin-to-cash divergence would weaken it.

3. **Breadth and documented historical financing execution — Analyst Interpretation.** CP-1A B02/B05–B07 and X06/BF02 support product/customer breadth and completed tenor extensions. These reduce isolated operating exposures and selected historical funding pressure. Common sector drivers and secured substitution remain counterevidence, while missing market inputs prevent extrapolating access. Better exposure detail and verified refinancing terms would improve confidence; concentrated order deterioration or materially more restrictive financing would reduce it.

**Weaknesses**

1. **Debt-funded extraction limits retained creditor cushion — Analyst Interpretation; Material risk.** CP-1A BF01/GT01/GT02 and CP-1 BS14 establish borrowing linked to a non-earning equity payout and a substantial accrued payment. The mechanism leaves debt service behind while removing cash, restricting the inference from gross base-date liquidity and elevating future capital-allocation monitoring. No FY2024/FY2023 buybacks, explicit reporting and historical extensions are credible contrary evidence, not reversal of the dividend. Sustained retention, restrained distributions and evidenced debt reduction would improve the view; further debt-funded shareholder returns would weaken it.

2. **Leverage leaves less tolerance for earnings or financing setbacks — Analyst Interpretation; Material risk.** CP-1 K07/K09 shows carrying debt and carrying leverage increased despite stronger earnings. In the downside chain, lower earnings or new borrowing would increase the burden on retained cash and refinancing. Improved operating-income/net-interest coverage (K11) is counterevidence, but is neither cash coverage nor covenant headroom. Accepted earnings, sustained cash retention and verified debt retirement would improve the view; persistent cash-funded shortfalls or incremental debt without contribution would weaken it.

3. **Acquisitions create competing cash demands and integration exposure — Analyst Interpretation; Material risk.** CP-1A X01/X02/GT03 and CP-1 CF24 show repeated acquisitions, including debt-linked CPI funding. New businesses may add earnings and diversification, but cash integration, preliminary allocations and uncertain contribution can postpone creditor benefit. Multiple added product exposures are genuine counterevidence to a purely adverse acquisition view. Demonstrated acquired cash returns and successful controls integration would improve it; acquisition-driven debt growth without realized contribution would weaken it.

4. **Sector and qualified-supply sensitivity can transmit into cash quickly — Analyst Interpretation; Material risk.** CP-1A B07/B10/B11/B14 supports utilization, OEM, budget, distributor and certification dependencies. Correlated volume declines or production constraints can reduce shipments, pressure mix and absorb inventory cash, weakening liquidity before management can fully adjust costs. Aftermarket content and customer/product breadth mitigate this mechanism. Stable end-use demand, qualified supply and collections would support the view; persistent order cancellations, inventory accumulation, labor disruption or contract remedies would weaken it. No current adverse event is inferred.

The ranking reflects supported mechanics, not numerical risk probabilities. Missing liquidity, market, ownership and legal inputs are separately recorded as gaps, not additional adverse behavior. CP-1A's bounded governance rubric is not reproduced as a CP-2 composite rating or independently rescored.

## Findings

### Legal assessment

**The supplied 2033 indenture combines meaningful payment, lien and voting protections with aggressive borrower flexibility in distributions, investments and legal earnings adjustments.** Its principal weakness is not a demonstrated covenant breach: it is the ability to remove or relocate value while satisfying transaction-based tests, including an unrestricted-payment route when legal fixed-charge coverage exceeds 2.0x. The strongest contrary evidence is the express junior-lien-or-Permitted-Lien rule, joint-and-several payment guarantees, affected-holder protection for ranking/payment changes and a two-thirds collateral/ICA consent threshold. Those protections can constrain an overt priority rewrite, but they do not eliminate expressly permitted leakage, releases or pari dilution. Exact capacity, perfection and enforcement control remain unproven without the missing package and transaction inputs.

This assessment is **Analyst Interpretation**, based on clause-level Documentary Facts below. It is instrument-specific, not a finding that all TransDigm debt has identical terms. Provisional covenant-aggressiveness assessment is **4/5, Aggressive**, not a market-relative grade. Confidence is Medium for credit implications and higher for the directly read wording; package-wide execution/compliance conclusions are not supported.

### Legal risks and protections

**Definitions change capacity, not just reported leverage.** L p.5 L410–L424 defines FCCR as legal EBITDA over Fixed Charges for four full quarters with internal statements, pro forma financing and acquisitions/dispositions, transaction-date floating rates and swap effects. Fixed Charges adds tax-grossed preferred dividends to defined interest. Defined interest excludes financing-fee amortization, bridge/commitment fees, qualified securitization costs and prepayment premiums, while adding capitalized interest and capital-lease interest. EBITDA includes expansive transaction, restructuring, dividend-equivalent and projected-savings adjustments. Clause M's 35% limit is neither a global cap on all EBITDA add-backs nor a cap on every pro forma acquisition adjustment: L421–L422 separately permits officer-good-faith acquisition calculations and reasonably determined operating expense reductions. The no-duplication and specified exclusions still matter; the document is not permission to add the same amount twice. Wider earnings and narrower fixed charges can make ratio debt and distributions easier before actual cash savings arrive, increasing debt-service sensitivity and weakening the residual asset cushion. Monitor adjustment categories, actual realization and transaction-date rate inputs, not the accounting multiple.

**Debt and lien permissions are separate.** L p.18 §4.09 L1295 says **“greater than 2.0 to 1.0”**, not greater than or equal. L p.10 L715 says **“shall not exceed 5.25 to 1.00”** for the specific (xxxi) Ratio Indebtedness lien route. Permitted Liens (iii) covers Bank Indebtedness; (xx) links purchase-money and additional-debt baskets to asset-specific/collateral-only limits; (xxi) confines foreign-sub liens to foreign-sub assets. Accordingly, 5.25 is not a blanket secured leverage maintenance ceiling or a condition on every lien. Permitted-debt reclassification can refresh fixed baskets; acquisition debt can use an improved-FCCR alternative even without satisfying the USD1 ratio-debt test. These provisions can permit further pari claims or locally senior funding without a new breach, but actual priming is not established. The contrary case is §4.12's express junior-or-permitted requirement and §9.02's affected-holder ranking protection. A proposed priority change must satisfy those boundaries and the missing ICA, rather than relying on a generic majority-vote claim.

**Leakage can occur before default and may outlast deteriorating tests.** §4.07 L1265 permits **“any Restricted Payment”** subject to no continuing Default/EoD and pro forma FCCR exceeding 2.0x. L1272 preserves certain payments contractually committed while conditions held. The builder basket therefore is not the sole potential distribution constraint. Permitted Investments can reach non-guarantors, and designation of a guarantor as Unrestricted can release its guarantee and liens under §§10.07(c),12.07(f), subject to designation and RP conditions. Asset-sale exclusions, §5.01's intragroup carveout and affiliate carveouts mean a transfer may avoid one covenant yet remain subject to others. No categorical IP-transfer prohibition is identified in the supplied indenture; this is a conditional route, not a finding that material IP has been transferred. Without an entity/IP schedule, valuation and usage ledger its amount is Not calculable. These mechanics can reduce creditors' reachable value without an immediate payment default; monitor designations, intragroup transfers, RP commitments and releases as well as reported dividends.

**The historical distribution demonstrates willingness, not a capacity opinion.** S1 p.131 expressly links September notes and Tranche L proceeds plus existing cash to the USD75/share declaration and eligible option equivalents. S1 p.146 records USD4,216 million common dividends accrued at September 30 and USD4,216 million common plus USD132 million equivalent payments in **October 2024**. The latter are subsequent cash uses, not FY2024 cash flow. Neither the funding link nor the issuer compliance statement on p.132 identifies the precise §4.07 route, verifies conditions at declaration/commitment or proves residual capacity. A general compliance assertion is not the missing transaction certificate. Retain CP-1A BF01 as extraction behavior, not unlawful payment or coercive LME evidence.

**Asset-sale protection is real but delayed and qualified.** FMV consideration and conditional cash requirements, reinvestment/application deadlines, and a pro rata 100%-plus-interest offer protect noteholders where §4.10 applies. Countervailing flexibility includes deemed cash (assumed liabilities, instruments converted within 180 days and designated noncash consideration), long reinvestment periods, net-proceeds deductions, use to repay secured or non-guarantor debt, and return of untendered residual to permitted general purposes. The special productive-assets alternative requires substitute Productive Assets promptly to become Collateral where sold assets were collateral (L1317). This supports collateral continuity in that path, but is not a universal requirement that all proceeds immediately repay these Notes. Do not collapse asset-sales proceeds into near-term note amortization.

**Guarantees improve direct recourse but are neither universal nor permanent.** §10.01 promises unconditional, irrevocable, joint-and-several payment/performance, not merely collection, with reinstatement for rescinded payments; §10.02 limits enforceability by fraudulent-transfer law. The executed signer list includes CPI, Calspan, Raptor entities and TransDigm UK, among others (L pp.31–32), but is not a current exhaustive ownership/value schedule. §4.17's facility limb and separate >=200 capital-markets limb can capture new obligors, with 20-Business-Day accession; §12.04 links required guarantee accession to security/ICA joinder. §10.07 nonetheless releases on permitted external disposals, compliant USub designation, immateriality under its conditions, release from specified triggering debt, or funded discharge/defeasance. Immaterial Domestic Restricted Subsidiary requires both <=2.5% EBITDA and <=2.5% assets, using the specified >45-day reporting lag (L p.7 L535); no aggregate immateriality cap is stated in that definition. A non-guarantor is not the same as an Unrestricted Subsidiary, and a foreign subsidiary is not automatically outside every guarantee: TransDigm UK is expressly excluded from the defined Foreign Restricted Subsidiary category and signs here.

**Security documentation determines realized control.** Collateral excludes the absent Security Agreement's Excluded Collateral (L p.4 L389). §12.03 conditions some further collateralization on corresponding facility requirements; §12.06 provides commercially reasonable perfection efforts and a 90-day outside period, not evidence those filings were completed. §12.07(e)(B) follows specified Credit Agreement Collateral Agent releases, but excludes the stated full-cash facility discharge outside foreclosure/remedies; it is not an automatic release whenever the facility is repaid. §12.07(e)(A) can release collateral transferred outside Company/Holdings/Guarantors in a permitted transaction, potentially including a restricted non-guarantor recipient, subject to full operative conditions. Permitted automatic releases differ from amendments releasing substantially all collateral outside the documents. Certificates and opinions are required to evidence requested releases; none is supplied here.

**LME/control protection is mixed rather than absent.** §9.02 expressly contemplates consents in tender/exchange offers; general covenant changes can bind dissenters by majority. However, affected-holder protections include principal, fixed maturity, redemption terms, interest/payment timing, currency, payment suit, adversely changed ranking and specified post-trigger change-of-control obligations. L p.27 L1857 protects changes **“affecting the subordination or ranking of the Notes or the Guarantees”** adverse to holders. A materially adverse ICA modification or unauthorized all/substantially all collateral release needs 66⅔%, not merely majority. §2.09 excludes issuer/control-affiliate votes, with trustee actual-knowledge protection. §6.06 prohibits using the indenture to obtain preference over another holder; §6.07 preserves individual due-payment suits. These are meaningful opposite-case barriers. They do not prove that every non-pro-rata exchange, open-market purchase or asset-based transaction is prohibited, or that a majority can validly override every priority right. No executed coercive LME, uptier or drop-down is established by the supplied actions.

#### Default detail, suspension and funded exit

Payment/nonpayment and notice conditions must not be conflated. Interest gets 30 days (§6.01(a)); principal and due tender payments do not receive that same grace (§6.01(b)). Other covenants require notice from trustee or 25% holders and 60 days, reporting 180 days; §5.01 requires notice but not that passage of time (§6.01(c)). Cross-debt default is a **final-maturity payment failure or acceleration**, not every debt covenant breach; threshold is at least USD50 million and excludes Securitization Entities in that limb. Final/nonappealable judgments use **in excess of** USD50 million and a 60-day unpaid/unstayed test. Collateral failure above USD50 million has a 60-day persistence limb, while a court pleading repudiating validity is separately covered (§6.01(h)). The Company or Significant Subsidiary insolvency events are covered, but automatic acceleration under the controlling §6.02 applies to **Company** bankruptcy events; others use the stated declaration mechanism. Majority can rescind acceleration under conditions and waive nonpayment-excepted past defaults; it cannot simply waive continuing ordinary payment defaults for all dissenters (§§6.02,6.04,6.07).

§4.19 requires both agencies' investment-grade ratings and no continuing Default for suspension. Suspended provisions include RP, upstream restrictions, incurrence, asset sales, affiliates, business, guarantees, preferred stock, impairment and specified merger ratio condition; **liens and change-of-control remain outside that list**. Reversion is prospective, with suspension-period debt allocated under its specified treatment, no retroactive breach solely for suspension-period acts and a 30-day catch-up guarantee accession. Actual suspension notices/ratings are Not supplied; no conclusion that covenants were switched off is made.

Article VIII defeasance is different from ratings suspension: irrevocable USD cash/noncallable government-securities funding sufficient in independent accountants' opinion, tax/legal opinions, officers' certificates, no-default and specified 91-day bankruptcy conditions are required. Covenant defeasance releases the listed covenants including lien/change-of-control obligations and specified cross-default/judgment events; legal defeasance discharges broader obligations with surviving trust-payment rights. ### Downside, loss mechanisms and strongest countercases

**Time-aware operating downside:** from the September 2024 base, weaker utilization or qualified-supplier disruption first reduces spares demand or deliverable shipments (CP-1A B10/B11/B14), then revenue/mix and margin (B04/B08), then collections and inventory conversion (B13; CP-1 K03). Interest, reinvestment and committed payouts compete for cash. Borrowing may initially bridge cash needs but raises claims; eligible A/R may tighten just when liquidity is needed. A July 2025 renewal requirement can matter before longer bond maturities, but no outcome is inferred from the missing follow-up. Notes need not suffer an immediate numerical maintenance breach simply because earnings fall. Transaction incurrence/RP permissions, payment default rules and refinancing access are distinct pathways (CP-4 F01/F13).

**Economic loss versus legal loss:** spread widening or rates rising can create mark-to-market loss before any default. Fixed longer notes face duration plus credit-spread repricing; floating loans can have less fixed-rate duration but credit discount and exit-liquidity risk, while higher floating service costs affect issuer cash. In a later restructuring, lower enterprise/pool values, senior dilution, leakage, costs and realization delay reduce distributable proceeds; subordination makes juniors more convex to residual shortfall. A bond's par shortfall is not the investor's entry-price loss: economic loss depends on purchase price, proceeds, interim cash and timing, all of which are missing here. No assumed recovery floor, stress magnitude, PD or portfolio loss is assigned.

**Economic countercase:** installed-base replacement demand, improving historical conversion and completed extensions may allow retained cash to reduce refinancing dependence. It would win if subsequent comparable financial evidence showed recurring conversion after maintenance/integration needs, actual debt retirement and restrained discretionary payouts. That would improve all claims, potentially letting discounted subordinated debt outperform on price; it still needs verified compensation and residual support.

**Legal countercase:** guarantees, intended first-priority liens, junior-or-permitted conditions and sacred voting rights may preserve more reachable value than the leakage-risk narrative suggests. It would win if the full executed package, filings, entity map and transaction certificates demonstrate retained collateral, enforceable coverage and constrained competing claims. This would raise conviction in the secured protection case, not mechanically establish its fair spread.

**Structural countercase:** a senior label does not ensure superior investment outcome if assets sit in excluded/non-guarantor pools, agents cannot realize value promptly or price already discounts almost no loss. Conversely, enforceable junior guarantees and a sufficiently low entry price could compensate for subordination. Verified entity values, competing claims and comparable prices would decide; missing documents do not prove the adverse structural case. These countercases keep structural preference conditional and implementation withheld rather than converting gaps into Avoid decisions.

## Analytical depth — binding on every run

Compressed from `../../CANON_SHARED.md § CP_AB_EXPORT_SPEC.md`. Restated inline because
it binds every run, and canon is opened only to resolve a named ambiguity.

1. **Complete every workflow step** in this prompt and its invoked method companions, and
   represent each material step in the reader-facing synthesis or a governed appendix
   register. A populated minimum register set is not proof the whole workflow ran.
2. **Express every material conclusion as an issuer-specific chain** — evidence and
   locator → risk mechanic → creditor implication. Naming a metric, framework category or
   generic risk without the transmission mechanism is incomplete.
3. **Identify the strongest supported contrary evidence or counterargument and explain
   what would make it win.** Where this module informs a decision, state how that
   challenge changes conviction, implementation or monitoring.
4. **Make downside causal and time-aware**: initiating condition, first operational break,
   financial transmission, liquidity/leverage/refinancing consequence, observable trigger.
   A generic recession paragraph or an unsupported stress number is incomplete.
5. **Reconcile disagreements across sources, periods, definitions and analytical modules
   explicitly.** Where evidence cannot resolve one, preserve it as a gap and reduce
   confidence; never smooth it into a single narrative.
6. **Use frameworks only when they change the credit conclusion**, translated into
   creditor consequences rather than listed as labels.

Depth is evidence-proportionate: missing evidence produces explicit gaps and bounded
conclusions, never shorter reasoning or invented filler.

## Absorbed phase — CP-5A, binding on every CP-5 run

CP-5 absorbs the research-integrity grade — severity rules, QA status, and whether committee use is permitted, restricted or blocked. Tracing the evidence and grading what the trace found are one verdict, and a committee reads them as one. CP-5A is no longer a separate stage or a separate artifact: its registers are merged into CP-5's single output contract above and are authored on every CP-5 run. `Run CP-5A` still dispatches here and resolves to CP-5's artifact.

## Deterministic computation

These figures are script-owned. Run the script, transcribe its output, and do not hand-derive a value it produces — a hand-derived figure in a script-owned cell is a QA failure, not a rounding difference. Inputs and outputs stay canonical Markdown; the scripts read the tagged registers already in the handoff.

- `./scripts/confidence_score.py` — owns the Confidence Score, its band and the derived `qa_status`, per `../../CANON_SHARED.md § CP_CONFIDENCE_SCORE.md`. Classify each material claim's lineage and each finding's severity yourself, then pass the counts. Run it before authoring the register it feeds.
- `./scripts/completeness_check.py` — owns the mechanical half of QA: every required register present, declared columns present, minimum row counts met, and no disqualifying placeholder in a critical column. It reads this SKILL.md as the contract, so it cannot drift from it. Run it after drafting the complete handoff and before final validation/export; correct reported failures and rerun.

For CP-3 loan-market claims, apply `../../CANON_SHARED.md § Maintained loan-market reference — CP-3`: Sector RV is current and relevant by policy. ## Instructions
1. Inventory all upstream module canonical Markdown handoff `.md` files available for QA.
2. For each module: record Module, Handoff canonical `.md` / run_id, Scope, Source Quality, Envelope / Headings Status (YAML front-matter fields present + canonical H2 headings present), QA Status (pre-audit), and Notes.
3. Confirm CP-5 evidence trace is available.
4. Assess source quality and handoff envelope/heading completeness for each module (missing front-matter fields or canonical headings are gate findings).
5. Assign Module Status:
   - **Completed:** All target modules available with complete canonical Markdown envelopes and canonical headings.
   - **Ready with Limitations:** Some modules available but with incomplete handoff envelopes/headings, incomplete source packages, or CP-5 trace unavailable.
   - **Blocked:** No upstream module canonical Markdown handoffs available for audit. Output blocked message and STOP.

## REF_CP-5A_AuditRules.md

<reference module="CP-5A" name="Severity Escalation, Audit Lanes & Clearance">

Authoritative for CP-5A across all eight audit lanes (Steps 2–8) and the clearance decision (Steps 9–11). Load alongside the CP-5A workflow. The Severity Engine (qa_status mapping) stays in the ACTIVE_PROMPT.

## Severity Escalation Rules
**Escalate to Critical when defect affects:**
- Credit conclusion, investment recommendation, action bias, security selection, position sizing, or committee decision
- Legal meaning, contractual interpretation, recovery ranking, or creditor rights
- Economics, leverage, liquidity, FCF, debt service capacity, maturity profile, or refinancing capacity
- A calculation error that changes a material metric by more than a rounding threshold
- A fabricated, unsourced, or materially misleading claim in committee-facing output

**Escalate to Material when defect affects:**
- Evidence traceability, source quality disclosure, or limitation transparency
- Cross-module inconsistency in material metrics or conclusions
- Structured export integrity or database ingestion
- Required monitoring trigger or remediation action omission
- Source-quality limitation that is not disclosed

**Keep as Minor when:**
- Formatting, duplication, clarity, table hygiene, or non-core presentation issue
- Does not impair interpretation, source support, credit conclusion, or downstream ingestion

## 8 Audit Lanes
| Lane | Scope | Key Severity Trigger |
|------|-------|---------------------|
| 1. Unsupported Claim | All material factual, numerical, legal, comparative, recovery, market, sponsor/governance, and committee-relevant claims | Critical if thesis-changing |
| 2. Calculation | All formulas, metrics, ratios, financial/capacity/headroom calculations, derived figures | Critical if changes material metric |
| 3. Legal / Covenant | All covenant, basket, lien, debt-incurrence, RP, investment, asset-transfer, guarantee, collateral, intercreditor, ranking, recovery, amendment, LME claims | Critical if affects creditor rights/recovery/legal meaning |
| 4. Market / RV | All price, spread, yield, DM, trading level, comparable, ranking, rating, benchmark, security-selection, RV claims | Critical if changes recommendation |
| 5. Cross-Module Consistency | All shared data points: issuer name, entity keys, EBITDA, leverage, liquidity, maturities, covenant capacity, recovery, market data, recommendations, monitoring posture | Critical if contradictory conclusions |
| 6. Evidence Trace | CP-5 evidence trace outputs and source lineage for all material conclusions | Critical if orphan claim is thesis-changing |
| 7. Schema | canonical Markdown handoff YAML front-matter envelope fields, schema versions, required fields, null-not-zero compliance | Critical if breaks the handoff envelope |
| 8. Handoff Envelope | Canonical Markdown completeness: YAML envelope + all canonical H2 headings present; the Markdown handoff exist, have matching filenames, and pass view-appropriate parity | Critical if breaks the agent-to-agent handoff |

## Evidence Support Classification
Supported | Partially Supported | Unsupported | Conflicting | Insufficient Information

## Defect Categories (23)
Unsupported Claim | Partially Supported Claim | Conflicting Evidence | Citation Gap | Source Quality Limitation | Calculation Error | Formula / Definition Drift | Period Mismatch | Entity / Perimeter Mismatch | Legal Support Gap | Covenant / Basket Overreach | Recovery / Ranking Overreach | Market Data Gap | Relative Value Unsupported | Cross-Module Inconsistency | Version Conflict | Duplicative / Immaterial Content | Promotional or Non-Credit Language | canonical Markdown Handoff Integrity Defect | Evidence Trace Defect | Markdown/export Consistency Defect | Gate Compliance Breach | Safety / Scope Breach

## Clearance Impact Labels (9)
Blocks Committee Use | Restricts Committee Use | Blocks canonical Markdown Handoff / Downstream Grounding | Requires Legal Review | Requires Market Data Refresh | Requires Calculation Rebuild | Requires Source Reconciliation | Monitoring Follow-Up | Formatting / Hygiene Only

## Calculation Audit Requirements
A calculation is QA-usable only if it includes ALL of: formula, numerator, denominator, period, units/currency, source trace, normalization/pro forma adjustments, sign convention, reconciliation to module output. If any element is missing → Not Calculable from Provided Materials (unless missing element is immaterial and limitation disclosed).

## Committee Clearance Logic
- **Pass:** No Critical issues and no unresolved Material issues affecting committee use or export integrity.
- **Pass with Remediation:** No unresolved Critical issues, but ≥1 Material or Minor issues require correction or limitation disclosure.
- **Fail:** ≥1 unresolved Critical issues, missing auditable output, inability to identify issuer/entity, or defects that block committee use.

## Role (relocated from ACTIVE_PROMPT 2026-07-11)
You are a forensic research-governance auditor for leveraged-finance research outputs. **Your input is each upstream module's canonical Markdown handoff `.md`** — the YAML front-matter envelope plus the canonical H2 headings (`## Audit Summary`, `## Analysis`, `## Evidence Trace`, `## Source Registry`, `## Gaps & Conflicts`, `## QA Validation`) — attached as grounding. You read these handoffs directly; you do NOT parse `.docx` JSON appendices and there is no CP-EXTRACT. Your role is to determine whether those module outputs are source-supported, internally consistent, calculation-safe, legally disciplined, handoff-compliant, and suitable for senior credit committee consumption. You do NOT rewrite the investment thesis or create new issuer analysis. You audit, classify, gate, and clear. Assume prior outputs

# CP-5 | Discipline Reference

## Prohibited Behaviors — Full Binding List (relocated from ACTIVE_PROMPT 2026-07-11)
1. Do not fabricate source paths, page numbers, native citations, financial figures, LBO entry multiples, valuation, sources and uses, sponsor economics, ownership percentages, purchase price, leverage, maturity profile, debt quantum, revenue mix, customer concentration, operating KPIs, legal capacity, covenant terms, market prices, spreads, yields, discount margins, peer multiples, recovery assumptions, or portfolio constraints.
2. Do not silently repair missing or malformed citations.
3. Do not alter substantive conclusions from upstream modules.
4. Do not add new credit analysis unless required to explain why evidence lineage is or is not committee-ready.
5. Do not cite a source for a claim that is not explicitly supported by that source.
6. Do not reconcile conflicting sources silently — log the conflict.
7. Do not assign a formal rating unless explicitly instructed.
8. Do not assign relative-value labels unless an upstream module already produced them and source trace supports them.
9. If a required source is unavailable, do not fabricate the lineage; mark [Insufficient Information] and log the gap.

# CP-5 | Style and Format Reference

## Style (relocated from ACTIVE_PROMPT 2026-07-11)
Professional, neutral, concise, institutional, ratings-style, creditor-focused, audit-focused. Use concise paragraphs, dense bullets, and Excel-ready Markdown tables. Avoid generic adjectives ("market-leading," "robust," "strong," "resilient," "diversified," "ample," "cheap," "rich") unless immediately supported by issuer-specific evidence and credit implication. A dense, accurate sentence is preferred to broad generic commentary. 1–5 pages per issuer for Top 5 scope; scale for Full scope.

## Source and Citation Discipline (relocated from ACTIVE_PROMPT 2026-07-11)
- Quote exact source filenames where available.
- Every material factual claim, calculation, legal assertion, market datapoint, RV statement, recommendation, monitoring trigger, assumption, or committee-relevant conclusion must be traceable to a source or explicitly flagged.
- For calculated metrics, cite source files used for inputs and state the formula.
- If external sources are used by upstream modules, preserve the [External] label and trace where available.
- If multiple sources conflict, log the conflict rather than reconciling silently.
- If source quality is limited (stale, draft, incomplete, unaudited, management-adjusted, pro forma, non-comparable, promotional, or missing key schedules), state the limitation and downstream credit relevance.

## Input Method (relocated from ACTIVE_PROMPT 2026-07-11)
Read each upstream module's **canonical Markdown handoff `.md`** (YAML front-matter envelope + canonical H2 headings: `## Audit Summary`, `## Analysis`, `## Evidence Trace`, `## Source Registry`, `## Gaps & Conflicts`, `## QA Validation`) attached as grounding. Validate claim-to-source lineage directly from those handoffs and from CP-5A QA output — do NOT parse `.docx` JSON appendices or any extraction envelope (there is no CP-EXTRACT). Restate the exact `module_id` / `run_id` / `reporting_period` consumed.

## Role (relocated from ACTIVE_PROMPT 2026-07-11)
You are a research-governance analyst specializing in provenance, evidence-lineage, and auditability for leveraged-finance research outputs. Your role is to validate claim-to-source lineage — confirming that every material credit conclusion in upstream module outputs is traceable to an identified source, correctly classified, and committee-ready. You do NOT alter substantive credit conclusions, create new credit analysis, or silently repair missing citations. This is a governance layer only. Creditor / leveraged-finance research governance perspective.

## Confidence (relocated from ACTIVE_PROMPT 2026-07-11)
The primary confidence measure is the numeric **`confidence_score` (0–100)** computed per `the shared CP_CONFIDENCE_SCORE.md section` (do not invent a formula); the band (High / Medium / Low / Insufficient Information) is the derived label per that spec's band map. CP-5 recomputes / audits the score it emits.

## Content Distinctions (relocated from ACTIVE_PROMPT 2026-07-11)
Source Fact | Management / Marketing Language | Calculation | Analyst Interpretation | Assumption | Provenance Assessment | Credit Implication | Missing Information | Weak Lineage | Untraced Conclusion | Markdown/export Artifact Integrity Warning

## Traceability Scope Rules (relocated from ACTIVE_PROMPT 2026-07-11)
**Default scope:** Map the Top 5 most material credit drivers only.
**Full scope (user-requested):** Map all material conclusions affecting PD, LGD, liquidity, refinancing capacity, recovery, relative value, recommendation, monitoring, security selection, position sizing, portfolio action, or committee readiness.

## Orphan Claim Protocol (relocated from ACTIVE_PROMPT 2026-07-11)
**Definition:** A material conclusion where lineage_class is Untraced, Weak Lineage, or Insufficient Information AND appears in committee-facing output AND no mitigation/limitation_flag applied.
**Trigger:** VE-015 (ORPHAN_CLAIM)
**Severity:** Critical if the conclusion affects economics, legal meaning, recommendation, security selection, position sizing, committee decision, PD, LGD, recovery, refinancing, or relative value.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures
     We present below certain financial information based on our EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined.
References to “EBITDA” mean earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, and references to
“EBITDA As Defined” mean EBITDA plus, as applicable for each relevant period, certain adjustments as set
forth in the reconciliations of net income to EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined and the reconciliations of net
cash provided by operating activities to EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined presented below.

     Neither EBITDA nor EBITDA As Defined is a measurement of financial performance under U.S. GAAP.
We present EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined because we believe they are useful indicators for evaluating
operating performance and liquidity.

     Our management believes that EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined are useful as indicators of liquidity
because securities analysts, investors, rating agencies and others use EBITDA to evaluate a company’s ability to
incur and service debt. In addition, EBITDA As Defined is useful to investors because the revolving credit
facility under our senior secured credit facility requires compliance under certain circumstances, on a pro forma
basis, with a financial covenant that measures the ratio of the amount of our secured indebtedness to the amount
of our Consolidated EBITDA defined in the same manner as we define EBITDA As Defined herein.

     In addition to the above, our management uses EBITDA As Defined to review and assess the performance
of the management team in connection with employee incentive programs and to prepare its annual budget and
financial projections. Moreover, our management uses EBITDA As Defined to evaluate acquisitions.

     Although we use EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined as measures to assess the performance of our business
and for the other purposes set forth above, the use of these non-GAAP financial measures as analytical tools has
limitations, and you should not consider any of them in isolation, or as a substitute for analysis of our results of
operations as reported in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Some of these limitations are:
       •    neither EBITDA nor EBITDA As Defined reflects the significant interest expense, or the cash
           requirements, necessary to service interest payments on our indebtedness;
       •    although depreciation and amortization are non-cash charges, the assets being depreciated and
           amortized will often have to be replaced in the future, and neither EBITDA nor EBITDA As Defined
           reflects any cash requirements for such replacements;
       •    the omission of the substantial amortization expense associated with our intangible assets further limits
           the usefulness of EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined;
       •    neither EBITDA nor EBITDA As Defined includes the payment of taxes, which is a necessary element
           of our operations; and
       •    EBITDA As Defined excludes the cash expense we have incurred to integrate acquired businesses into
           our operations, which is a necessary element of certain of our acquisitions.

     Because of these limitations, EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined should not be considered as measures of
discretionary cash available to us to invest in the growth of our business. Management compensates for these
limitations by not viewing EBITDA or EBITDA As Defined in isolation and specifically by using other U.S.
GAAP measures, such as net income, net sales and operating profit, to measure our operating performance.
Neither EBITDA nor EBITDA As Defined is a measurement of financial performance under U.S. GAAP, and
neither should be considered as an alternative to net income or cash flow from operations determined in
accordance with U.S. GAAP. Our calculation of EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined may not be comparable to
the calculation of similarly titled measures reported by other companies.

15.   SEGMENTS
      The Company’s businesses are organized and managed in three reporting segments: Power & Control,
Airframe and Non-aviation.

      The Power & Control segment includes operations that primarily develop, produce and market systems and
components that predominately provide power to or control power of the aircraft utilizing electronic, fluid, power
and mechanical motion control technologies. Major product offerings include mechanical/electromechanical
actuators and controls, ignition systems and engine technology, specialized pumps and valves, power
conditioning devices, specialized AC/DC electric motors and generators, batteries and chargers, databus and
power controls, advanced sensor products, switches and relay panels, high performance hoists, winches and
lifting devices, cargo loading, handling and delivery systems and electronic components used in the generation,
amplification, transmission and reception of microwave signals. Primary customers of this segment are engine
and power system and subsystem suppliers, airlines, third party maintenance suppliers, military buying agencies
and repair depots. Products are sold in the original equipment and aftermarket market channels.

      The Airframe segment includes operations that primarily develop, produce and market systems and
components that are used in non-power airframe applications utilizing airframe and cabin structure technologies.
Major product offerings include engineered latching and locking devices, engineered rods, engineered connectors
and elastomer sealing solutions, cockpit security components and systems, specialized and advanced cockpit
displays, engineered audio, radio and antenna systems, specialized lavatory components, seat belts and safety
restraints, engineered and customized interior surfaces and related components, thermal protection and
insulation, lighting and control technology, parachutes, specialized flight, wind tunnel and jet engine testing
services and equipment and complex testing and instrumentation solutions. Primary customers of this segment
are airframe manufacturers and cabin system suppliers and subsystem suppliers, airlines, third party maintenance
suppliers, military buying agencies and repair depots. Products are sold in the original equipment and aftermarket
market channels.

      The Non-aviation segment includes operations that primarily develop, produce and market products for
non-aviation markets. Major product offerings include seat belts and safety restraints for ground transportation
applications, mechanical/electromechanical actuators and controls for space applications, hydraulic/
electromechanical actuators and fuel valves for land-based gas turbines, and refueling systems for heavy
equipment used in mining, construction and other industries and turbine controls for the energy and oil and gas
markets. Primary customers of this segment are off-road vehicle suppliers and subsystem suppliers, child
restraint system suppliers, satellite and space system suppliers, manufacturers of heavy equipment used in
mining, construction and other industries and turbine original equipment manufacturers, gas pipeline builders and
electric utilities.

segment is EBITDA As Defined. The Company defines EBITDA As Defined as earnings before interest, taxes,
depreciation and amortization plus certain non-operating items recorded as corporate expenses including
non-cash compensation charges incurred in connection with the Company’s stock incentive or deferred

17.   LEASES
      The Company leases certain manufacturing facilities, offices, land, equipment and vehicles. Such leases,
some of which are noncancellable and, in many cases, include renewals, expire at various dates. Such options to
renew are included in the lease term when it is reasonably certain that the option will be exercised. The
Company’s lease agreements typically do not contain any significant residual value guarantees or restrictive
covenants, and payments within certain lease agreements are adjusted periodically for changes in an index or
rate.

      The Company determines if an arrangement is a lease at inception. Operating lease assets and liabilities are
recognized at the commencement date of the lease based on the present value of lease payments over the lease
term. Lease assets represent the Company’s right to use an underlying asset for the lease term and lease liabilities
represent the Company’s obligation to make lease payments arising from the lease. The discount rate implicit
within our leases is generally not determinable and therefore we determine the discount rate based on our
incremental borrowing rate. The incremental borrowing rate for our leases is determined based on the lease term
and the currency in which lease payments are made. The length of a lease term includes options to extend or
terminate the lease when it is reasonably certain that the Company will exercise those options. The Company
made an accounting policy election to not recognize lease assets or liabilities for leases with a term of twelve
months or less. Additionally, when accounting for leases, the Company combines payments for leased assets,
related services and other components of a lease.

PART I
ITEM 1.   BUSINESS

The Company
      TD Group, through its wholly-owned subsidiary, TransDigm Inc., is a leading global designer, producer and
supplier of highly engineered aircraft components that are critical to the safe and effective operation of nearly all
commercial and military aircraft worldwide. Our products are represented in nearly every commercial and
military aircraft in service today. Our business is well diversified due to the broad range of products we offer to
our customers. We estimate that approximately 90% of our net sales for fiscal year 2024 were generated by
proprietary products.

      Most of our products generate significant aftermarket revenue. Once our parts are designed into and sold on
a new aircraft, we generate net sales from aftermarket consumption over the life of that aircraft, which is
generally estimated to be approximately 25 to 30 years. A typical platform can be produced for 20 to 30 years,
giving us an estimated product life cycle in excess of 50 years. We estimate that approximately 55% of our net
sales in fiscal year 2024 were generated from the aftermarket, the vast majority of which come from the
commercial and military aftermarkets. Historically, these aftermarket revenues have produced a higher gross
profit and have been more stable than net sales to original equipment manufacturers (“OEMs”).

      We believe we have achieved steady, long-term growth in sales and improvements in operating performance
we believe that due to our competitive strengths and through execution of our value-driven operating strategy.
More specifically, focusing our businesses on our value-driven operating strategy of obtaining profitable new
business, carefully controlling the cost structure via productivity and cost improvements and pricing our highly
engineered value-added products to fairly reflect the value we provide and the resources required to do so has
historically resulted in improvements in gross profit and income from operations over the long-term.

      We also maintain a selective acquisition strategy, concentrating on proprietary commercial aerospace
component businesses with significant aftermarket content, where we see a clear path to value creation. Since the
inception of our company in 1993, we have acquired 93 businesses and various product lines. Refer to Note 2,
“Acquisitions,” in the notes to the consolidated financial statements included herein for information on the recent
acquisitions.

Products
      We primarily design, produce and supply highly engineered proprietary aerospace components with
significant aftermarket content. We seek to develop highly customized products to solve specific needs for
aircraft operators and manufacturers. We attempt to differentiate ourselves based on engineering, service and
manufacturing capabilities. We typically choose not to compete for non-proprietary “build to print” business
because it frequently offers lower margins than proprietary products. We believe that our products have strong
brand names within the industry and that we have a reputation for high quality, reliability and strong customer
support. Our business is well diversified due to the broad range of products that we offer to our customers. Each
of our product offerings is composed of many individual products that are typically customized to meet the needs
of a particular aircraft platform or customer. Our portfolio of products encompasses a vast array of essential
components that play pivotal roles on commercial aerospace and defense platforms, as well as other products.
For example, TransDigm’s operating units make aircraft seatbelts and cockpit security systems that keep
passengers and pilots safe; parachutes that protect soldiers, sailors and airmen; and space telescope equipment
that helps the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (“NASA”) better understand the universe.

Segments
      The Company’s businesses are organized and managed in three reporting segments: Power & Control,
Airframe and Non-aviation.

                               Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm

To the Stockholders and the Board of Directors of
TransDigm Group Incorporated


Opinion on the Financial Statements
      We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of TransDigm Group Incorporated (the
“Company”) as of September 30, 2024 and 2023, the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive
income, changes in stockholders’ deficit and cash flows for each of the three fiscal years in the period ended
September 30, 2024, and the related notes and financial statement schedule listed in the Index at Item 15(a)
(collectively referred to as the “consolidated financial statements”). In our opinion, the consolidated financial
statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company at September 30, 2024
and 2023, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the three fiscal years in the period ended
September 30, 2024, in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.

      We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board
(United States) (“PCAOB”), the Company’s internal control over financial reporting as of September 30, 2024,
based on criteria established in Internal Control—Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring
Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework), and our report dated November 7, 2024
expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.


Basis for Opinion
      These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company’s management. Our responsibility is to
express an opinion on the Company’s financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm
registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with
the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange
Commission and the PCAOB.

      We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we
plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of
material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. Our audits included performing procedures to assess the
risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing
procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding
the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting
principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of
the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.


Critical Audit Matter
      The critical audit matter communicated below is a matter arising from the current period audit of the
financial statements that was communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee and that:
(1) relates to accounts or disclosures that are material to the financial statements and (2) involved our especially
challenging, subjective or complex judgments. The communication of the critical audit matter does not alter in
any way our opinion on the consolidated financial statements, taken as a whole, and we are not, by
communicating the critical audit matter below, providing a separate opinion on the critical audit matter or on the
accounts or disclosures to which it relates.

                  Valuation of goodwill
Description       As disclosed in Note 8, the Company had goodwill of $10.4 billion at September 30, 2024. As
of the            discussed in Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements, goodwill is tested for impairment
Matter            annually as of the first day of the fourth fiscal quarter, or more frequently, if an event occurs or
                  circumstances change that would more likely than not reduce fair value below carrying value. The
                  Company’s goodwill is initially assigned to its reporting units as of the acquisition date. The
                  Company first assesses qualitative factors to determine whether it is more likely than not that the
                  fair value of a reporting unit is less than its carrying value. If the Company determines the
                  qualitative assessment is not sufficient to conclude on whether it is more likely than not that the
                  fair value is less than the carrying value, a quantitative impairment test is performed. The
                  company may also elect to bypass the qualitative assessment and perform a quantitative test for
                  any or all reporting units. The Company performed a quantitative assessment on the goodwill at
                  14 of its reporting units. As part of the quantitative assessment, the Company determines the fair
                  value of the reporting units using a discounted cash flow valuation model.

                  Auditing management’s quantitative impairment assessment was complex and judgmental for
                  certain of the 14 reporting units due to the significant estimation required to determine fair value.
                  In particular, the fair value estimates were sensitive to significant assumptions, such as changes in
                  the discount rate, revenue growth rates and EBITDA margins, which are affected by expectations
                  about future market or economic conditions.

model prescribed in ASC 606. A substantial portion of the Company’s revenue is recorded at a point in time
basis. Revenue is recognized from the sale of products or services when obligations under the terms of the
contract are satisfied and control of promised goods or services have transferred to the customer. Control is
transferred when the customer has the ability to direct the use of and obtain benefits from the goods or services.
Revenue is measured at the amount of consideration the Company expects to be paid in exchange for goods or
services. Refer to Note 3, “Revenue Recognition,” for further information.

2023-07 requires all segment profit or loss and assets disclosures to be provided on an annual and interim basis.

years beginning one year later. Early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating this standard to
determine its impact on our disclosures.

nature. The ASU also requires entities to disclose their income tax payments (net of refunds) to international,
federal, and state and local jurisdictions. The standard makes several other changes to income tax disclosure
requirements. This standard is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2024, and requires
prospective application with the option to apply it retrospectively. Early adoption is permitted. The Company is
